concepts.definition: FOUNDATIONS is a Tier 1 member owning standing vocabulary; ontology, frame, authority, lineage and work-boundary objects; construction accounts and imports; P0–P6 commitments, foundation-to-law format and family index; composition, conservation, core results, conjunction and categorical demonstration requirements; and hypotheses.

grounding.quote:
Tier 1. Owns the vocabulary of standing (§1); the ontology, with the frame,
authority, lineage and work-boundary objects, the three accounts of a
construction, and the rule for imports between members (§2); the commitments P0 to P6 with their standing, the
foundation-to-law format with the standing of its consequences, and the
index of material families (§3); the algebra of composition and
conservation, the core result algebra, the conjunction of results and the
demonstration a categorical claim requires (§4); and the hypotheses (§5).

concepts.label: FOUNDATIONS

concepts.definition: A foundational claim is a commitment or hypothesis with exactly one standing: recovered, an adopted premise consolidating named source rules without treating them as proof; independent, an adopted premise argued by a case where other commitments hold and it fails; derived, a consequence with named premises; or hypothesis, unestablished by method clause or argument, not law and carried for falsification. This standing differs from result standing and successor disposition.
concepts.label: Foundational standing

concepts.definition: Four distinct joins are named: categorical join, a map between categories; composition boundary, a join between successive steps; join of results, closed results combined under one decision rule; and relation join, participant equality in an enclosing relation. An unqualified join in a result context means join of results.

grounding.quote: Four uses of "join" in this corpus are distinct

concepts.label: Join meanings

concepts.definition: Subject is the exact thing a claim, representation or transformation concerns, identified by inventory and bytes or semantic addresses. Representation is bytes, text, model or program standing for a subject; representation equality does not establish meaning equality. Interpretation is a declared representation-to-meaning contract in context, naming reliable distinctions and residuals. Context declares subject, definitions, basis and admissible observations under which interpretation holds.

grounding.quote: | Interpretation | a declared contract from representation to meaning within a context; says which distinctions a consumer may rely on and which are residual | P1 |

concepts.label: Subject, representation, interpretation and context

concepts.definition: Outcome U is a selected, owner-defined, directly verifiable state with an acceptance interval, against which transformation adequacy is judged. Object O is a subject with scoped identity (authority, kind, value), boundary, current state and declared material relations; identity survives admissible state and encoding changes.

grounding.quote:
| Outcome U | a selected, owner-defined, directly verifiable state with an acceptance interval; adequacy of a transformation is judged against it | P2 |
| Object O | a subject with scoped identity (authority, kind, value), a boundary, current state and declared material relations; identity survives admissible state and encoding change | P3 |

concepts.label: Outcome and object

concepts.definition: An actor performs a step within a declared envelope of context, attention, time and capability. Roles are occupied relations, not actor kinds; configurations determine which roles exist. A step is bounded work with intake, selected context, grant, execution and output. A step-produced fact is a judgment, residual, observation or authority decision that cannot be reacquired from declared sources; reproducible observations are excluded.

grounding.quote: | Step-produced fact | a judgment, residual, observation or authority decision produced by a step that cannot be re-acquired from declared sources; an observation reproducible from declared sources is re-acquirable and is not one | P0, P4b |

concepts.label: Actor, step and step-produced fact

concepts.definition: Claim is an assertion with subject, property, basis, witness relation and falsifier. Evidence is exact admitted observations or artifacts carrying provenance, subject identity, basis and scope; availability inside a frame creates neither semantic truth nor decision authority. Judgment is a recorded evaluation over an unchanged subject with evaluator, decision, evidence, scope and revising observation. Authority is identity-bearing permission to operate or dispose acceptance within scope.

grounding.quote: | Judgment | a recorded evaluation over an unchanged subject, with evaluator, decision, evidence, scope and revising observation | P6 |

concepts.label: Claim, evidence, judgment and authority

concepts.definition: Residual is material uncertainty, omission, loss or an unproven relation remaining until authorised disposition. Basis is every exact version, identity, time, topology, authority, configuration or evidence coordinate whose change can alter a bound step, claim, result or evaluation. Basis is immutable or moving with declared advancement detection and reevaluation condition; mixed bases require an explicit composite relation. Materiality is evaluation-relative: lawful change can change result, basis validity, admissible evidence, permitted material operator or decision owner; the same criterion applies to uncertainty and closure.

grounding.quote: | Residual | a material uncertainty, omission, loss or unproven relation that remains until an authorised disposition | P4b |

concepts.label: Residual, basis and materiality

concepts.definition: Evaluation is a declared question with known admissible result family, evidence basis, decision authority and, when it performs material action, operation authority. It may seek judgment, prediction, construction, comparison, proof, refusal, classification or action recommendation. An evaluation family requires the same material-relation manifold, authority basis and result algebra; similar wording does not establish common family membership.

grounding.quote: | Evaluation family | evaluations that need the same material-relation manifold, authority basis and result algebra; similar wording does not prove that two evaluations share a family | P1, P2 |

concepts.label: Evaluation and evaluation family

concepts.definition: Workspace is the bounded material reasoned over or acted upon, potentially including sources, assets, designs, implementation, tools, runtime state, evidence, history, dependencies and human decisions; a repository is only one carrier. Material-relation manifold is the finite jointly interpretable set of needed variables, entities, identities, states, relations, invariants, authorities, observations and exclusions; overlapping charts imply neither geometric mathematics nor a runtime abstraction. Coordinate is the complete local basis, identity, lineage, input, evidence and authority position required for interpretation; equality follows a declared relation, not equal names, values, shapes, locations or apparent topology. Topology is the basis-specific structure of material entities, capabilities, authorities, lifecycle spaces, adjacencies and seams visible to a frame, which need not contain the full workspace topology.

grounding.quote: | Coordinate | the complete local position from which a value, event, decision, observation or action is interpreted: the basis, identity, lineage, input, evidence and authority information the evaluation requires; equal names, values, shapes, locations or apparent topology positions do not establish coordinate equality, which follows a declared relation | P1, P3 |

concepts.label: Workspace, manifold, coordinate and topology

concepts.definition: Capability envelope comprises competence, context capacity, tools, access, applicable evaluation or assurance independence and configuration needed to activate a frame and perform its evaluations. A reference frame is a finite specification of attention, coordinates, authority, evidence and result relations for one evaluation family on a basis. An activated frame binds a declaration to exact evaluation, workspace subject, basis, actor and evidence-acquisition boundary; a reusable declaration is not evidence of correct activation.

grounding.quote: | Activated frame | one frame declaration bound to an exact evaluation, workspace subject, basis, actor and evidence-acquisition boundary; a reusable declaration is not evidence that a particular activation was correct | P3, P6 |

concepts.label: Reference frame, activated frame and capability envelope

concepts.definition: Frame set is a human-declared family available for a governed outcome or workspace. Active frame configuration is the frame activations and declared result relations used for one evaluation or decision. Lens is a reusable question family, becoming a frame only with bounded evaluation, basis, manifold, evidence, authorities, result algebra and envelope. A role allocates responsibility or authority only through admitted grant; persona changes approach or salience; abstraction hides or contracts detail; component is a structural part. None is a frame by identity alone; components and frames may cross one another.

grounding.quote: | Lens | a reusable family of questions applied across a frame configuration; authority, capability and reuse, temporal behaviour, transport and proof are lenses when named abstractly; a lens becomes a frame only when instantiated with a bounded evaluation, basis, material manifold, evidence, authorities, result algebra and capability envelope | P2 |

concepts.label: Frame set, configuration, lens and adjacent roles

concepts.definition: Frame-set authority is human authority declaring or accepting a project frame set; semantic authority owns material-relation meaning; evaluation authority permits evaluation; operation authority is an owner-issued grant to construct, transform, admit, publish or mutate a material subject; decision authority permits accepting, rejecting or otherwise disposing a result. Actor identity is the performing human, agent, tool or process, not authority. Kinds may lawfully coincide but never collapse by default.

grounding.quote:
These may coincide in a lawful case and
never collapse by default.

concepts.label: Authority kinds

concepts.label: Bounded proxy

concepts.definition: Frame disjointness is structural absence of shared material variables, coordinates, evidence or result dependencies for declared evaluations. Evaluation independence is procedural separation of activated evaluations from one another's unclosed working results. Assurance independence is claim-relative non-authorship, evidence-acquisition, reference-exposure, actor and configuration separation required by governing assurance law.

concepts.label: Disjointness and independence

concepts.definition: The reference-frame tuple is ⟨Q, B, M, C, I, A, E, X, R, J, K, D⟩: evaluation family; workspace/topology basis; material manifold; coordinate/equality law; applicable invariants; authority relation; admissible evidence/provenance law; exclusions/prohibited assumptions; closed result algebra or core-mapped refinement; invalidation/rechart condition; actor envelope; and optional declared inter-frame dependencies, overlaps, inputs and outputs. It specifies an evaluation relation and finite attention scope, not a mandatory schema or runtime carrier.

concepts.definition: Construction realises a selected outer contract through steps. Its distinct accounts are algorithmic description (steps), informational interpretation (data meaning under an Interpretation), and computational realisation (people/machines carrying it out in a declared environment; a build tenant uses SPEC_METHOD §11's environment). This distinction applies to every construction independently of corpus tiers; a construction may need all three and none is a tier. It is an added choice owned by the corpus Product's Intent in its Direction, not a commitment and without foundational standing.

the steps, the meaning of

concepts.definition: Semantic import is reference-only use of another member's concept without redefining it: source and target meanings are identical owner-qualified references, directed from named source to importing context, with no loss, translation, ownership transfer or authority grant. Adoption takes the imported concept into use under source-owned adoption premises; lifecycle and adoption remain source-owned.

grounding.quote:

reference-only. Source and target meanings are identical owner-qualified
references, not new local definitions. Direction is from the named source
to the importing context; loss is none and no translation or ownership
transfer is asserted.

concepts.definition: P0 Bounded construction is recovered; P1 Interpretation, P2 Purpose, P3 Identity, P4a Typed composition and P6 Justification and authority are independent adopted premises. These domain-adopted premises are not theorems from finite capacity; particular rules also need owner-bound domain and policy choices.

concepts.definition: Construction synthesis relates the commitments to movement from observed current state to acceptable destination under finite resources. It is a derived consequence, not an additional commitment; ACTIVATION §1 owns the construction relation. Contributions are bounded acquisition/work and internal freedom (P0); preservation of meaning across conditions, observations and predictions (P1); selected Z and adequacy criteria (P2); persistent subject, observations and dependencies distinct from accounts (P3); obligations through refinement and composition boundaries (P4a); conservation through observation/correction/reuse (P4b); accounted resource tradeoffs, recursive progress, recovery and truthful undecided stops (P5); and established support and authority to model, act or accept (P6).

grounding.quote:

commitment, and has the standing of a consequence under Foundation to law
below
